title: Registration
outcomes: Identify compulsory registration and exempt persons.
Apply procedure, deemed approval and special categories.
Apply amendment, cancellation and revocation provisions.

meta.exam_tip: Check section 24 first; if not triggered, test the threshold.

concepts.title: Threshold-based registration
body: Section 22: every supplier must register in each State or UT from which it makes taxable supplies if aggregate turnover in a financial year exceeds ₹20 lakh (₹10 lakh in special category States — Manipur, Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura).

Suppliers exclusively of goods may enjoy ₹40 lakh in most States (not in Telangana, Puducherry and some north-eastern and hill States, where ₹20 lakh applies), provided they do not supply ice cream, pan masala or tobacco and are not required to register compulsorily.

Aggregate turnover is computed on an all-India PAN basis and includes taxable, exempt, export and inter-State supplies but excludes inward RCM supplies, taxes and supplies of non-taxable goods like alcohol; supplies of an agent on behalf of principals are included in the agent's turnover.
concepts.analogy: Turnover thresholds: ₹20 lakh generally, ₹40 lakh for goods-only, ₹10 lakh in special States.
concepts.work: A UP supplier of goods and services with ₹55 lakh turnover must register.

concepts.title: Compulsory registration and persons not liable
body: Section 24 requires registration irrespective of turnover for: inter-State taxable suppliers of goods (with exemptions for certain handicrafts and small sellers via ECOs); casual taxable persons; persons liable under reverse charge; ECOs liable under section 9(5); non-resident taxable persons; TDS deductors and TCS collectors; agents and ISDs; suppliers through ECOs that collect TCS (with exceptions for small service suppliers and notified goods suppliers); OIDAR suppliers from abroad to unregistered persons; and others notified.

Section 23 excludes persons engaged only in exempt or non-taxable supplies, agriculturists for produce from cultivation, and persons notified (e.g. suppliers liable only under RCM as recipients may still need to register).
Voluntary registration is allowed under section 25(3), with all obligations of a registered person.
concepts.analogy: Some activities need registration from the first rupee.
concepts.work: A Delhi trader making ₹5 lakh of inter-State sales must register.

concepts.title: Procedure, deemed approval and special categories
body: Section 25: apply within 30 days of becoming liable (casual and non-resident taxable persons at least 5 days before starting business) in Form GST REG-01, with PAN (except non-residents) and Aadhaar authentication; one registration per State, with separate registrations allowed for multiple places.

If Aadhaar authentication is done and no notice is issued, the application is deemed approved within 7 working days; with biometric verification or physical verification, deemed approval comes within 30 days if no notice is issued. Registration is effective from the date of liability if applied within 30 days.

Casual and non-resident taxable persons get registration valid up to 90 days (extendable by 90 days) and must deposit advance tax equal to estimated liability. A Unique Identity Number is given to UN bodies and embassies (section 25(9)).
concepts.analogy: Apply within 30 days; Aadhaar authentication speeds approval.
concepts.work: An exhibitor from another State registers as a casual taxable person 5 days before the fair.

concepts.title: Amendment, cancellation and revocation
body: Section 28: core field changes (name, place of business, partners) need approval within 15 days; non-core fields are updated online.

Section 29: cancellation may be sought by the person (business discontinued, transferred, change of constitution, no longer liable) or ordered by the officer for contravention, non-filing of returns (composition: beyond three months of the annual return due date; others: specified continuous periods), failure to start business within six months of voluntary registration, or registration obtained by fraud. Suspension may apply pending cancellation. On cancellation, tax equal to ITC on stock and capital goods (or output tax, if higher) must be paid.
Section 30: revocation of an officer-initiated cancellation can be sought within 90 days of service of the order, extendable by up to 180 days, after filing pending returns and paying dues.
concepts.analogy: Cancellation has a cost; revocation has strict time limits.
concepts.work: A cancelled dealer has up to 270 days in all to seek revocation.

jobs.title: Registration health check
jobs.situation: A start-up selling online across India asks if and where to register.
steps: Compute aggregate turnover on PAN basis.
Check section 24 triggers like inter-State supply and ECO TCS.
Register in each State of supply.
Plan Aadhaar authentication for fast approval.

viva.q: Which States have a ₹10 lakh threshold?
A trader crossed the threshold on 1 June and applied on 20 June. From when is the registration effective?
viva.model: From 1 June, the date of liability, because the application was within thirty days.

viva.q: What tax is payable on cancellation of registration?
viva.model: An amount equal to ITC on stock, semi-finished and finished goods and capital goods, or output tax on them, whichever is higher.

viva.q: Who receives a Unique Identity Number?
viva.model: UN bodies, embassies and other notified persons for refund of taxes on inward supplies.

viva.q: Is a person making only exempt supplies liable to register?
viva.model: Such a person falls outside the liability under section 23.

cases.title: Asha Crafts
cases.case: Asha Crafts, Rajasthan, sells handmade décor only within the State through its shop (₹18 lakh) and also through an e-commerce operator that collects TCS (₹4 lakh, intra-State).

mcqs.q: Is Asha liable on threshold basis if it supplies only goods (limit ₹40 lakh)?
mcqs.explain: Below ₹40 lakh. In practice: check State.

mcqs.q: Selling through an ECO that collects TCS generally triggers:
mcqs.explain: Section 24(ix). In practice: notified exemptions exist.
